s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital heart disease with severe right-sided cardiac dilation and left-sided hypoplasia, presenting with progressive dyspnea and cyanosis
salient_findings: Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
Severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting
key_facts: 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf
Progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency
Temperature 38.5 °C
Heart rate 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
Respiratory rate 60 breaths/min
Jugular pulses present
Mucous membranes cyanotic, especially after brief exertion
Grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
Harsh bronchovesicular lung sounds
Sinus tachycardia at 170 beats/min on electrocardiography
Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
Markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with severely reduced mitral valve orifice
16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum
Two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle

shortlist.label: Double Outlet Right Ventricle
shortlist.why_kept: Two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and interatrial and interventricular defects

shortlist.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with severely reduced mitral valve orifice and severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle

shortlist.label: Tricuspid Atresia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and right-sided cardiac dilation, although tricuspid atresia typically presents with more pronounced right ventricular hypoplasia

shortlist.label: Double Outlet Unventricular Heart
shortlist.why_kept: Similarities with double outlet right ventricle, but consideration of univentricular heart due to hypoplastic left ventricle and presence of interatrial and interventricular defects

shortlist.label: Taussig-Bing Anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to double outlet right ventricle, with two great vessels arising from the right ventricle, but typically involves subpulmonary ventricular septal defect

raw.rationale: The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and a hypoplastic left ventricle with reduced mitral valve orifice are consistent with Double Outlet Right Ventricle, which is characterized by both great arteries originating from the right ventricle.

rejected.label: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
rejected.why: While there is a hypoplastic left ventricle, the presence of two great vessels arising from the right ventricle does not align with the typical anatomy of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, where the left ventricle is underdeveloped and the aorta is often severely hypoplastic.

rejected.label: Tricuspid Atresia
rejected.why: Tricuspid Atresia involves an absence or abnormality of the tricuspid valve, which is not the primary issue described; instead, severe tricuspid regurgitation and the specific great vessel anatomy point away from this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Double Outlet Unventricular Heart
rejected.why: This condition involves one ventricle supporting both circulations, which is not clearly indicated here as there's mention of both right and left ventricles, albeit with significant anomalies.

rejected.label: Taussig-Bing Anomaly
rejected.why: A specific type of Double Outlet Right Ventricle, but the description provided does not specifically align with the characteristic subpulmonary ventricular septal defect and the aorta's position anterior to the pulmonary artery seen in Taussig-Bing Anomaly.
